title: ECB Economic Bulletin Issue 6, 2026 — the comprehensive edition carrying the September staff projections' integrated discussion
source: EST: ecb.europa.eu Economic Bulletin index (press/economic-bulletin/html/index.en.html), re-fetched direct 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200) — the page states the schedule verbatim, the Bulletin is 'released eight times a year, two weeks after each monetary policy meeting', and names the next release outright: 'Issue 6, 2026 - 24 September 2026'. Same page: the March/June/September/December editions are the comprehensive ones carrying an 'integrated discussion of the staff macroeconomic projections on inflation, growth, public finances, and external trade'. MEASURED against the ECB's own all-releases archive (press/economic-bulletin/html/all_releases.en.html, fetched direct 2026-09-08) rather than taken on the rule's word: across the 13 editions published 2025-02-13 through 2026-08-06, publication minus meeting Day 2 is exactly 14 days in 9, exactly 15 days in 3, and 28 days in 1 — and every exception is mechanical rather than discretionary. All three 15-day cases land where Day 2 + 14 fell on a Frankfurt public holiday (2025-05-01 Labour Day, 2025-06-19 Corpus Christi in Hesse, 2026-05-14 Ascension Day) and shifted exactly one business day; the single 28-day case is the year-end edition (2025-12-18 meeting, Issue 8 published 2026-01-15), whose +14 would have been New Year's Day. 2026-09-10 + 14 = 2026-09-24, a Thursday with no German public holiday, so the stated date and the rule agree with no exception available. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy carries no slot for a non-Fed central bank — the same taxonomy reason ecb-decision-2026-09-10 and ecb-account-2026-10-08 are both filed estimate despite direct ECB primaries. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-08 by the ecb-decision-2026-09-10 D-2 pulse-check adjacency sweep (proposals/ecb-economic-bulletin-2026-09-24.from-ecb-decision-2026-09-10.json, now shadowed by this canonical file); researched the same day. Impact LOW and symbols empty, and this event's own initial research is what substantiates that rather than the parent's assertion. Measured over the same 13 editions: raw close-to-close |move| on publication days runs 1.25x baseline for the Euro Stoxx 50 and 1.46x for the DAX — which LOOKS like an event until the US session is subtracted, at which point the euro-minus-SPX residual is 0.95x and 0.91x baseline, i.e. BELOW an ordinary day. The elevated raw number is imported global beta on days the Bulletin merely happened to share, and VIX level on publication days (18.76) is indistinguishable from the 2025-26 baseline (18.75). Mechanism behind the null, from an ECB primary: Issue 4 2026 states 'The cut-off date for the statistics included in this issue was 10 June 2026' for a 25 June publication — the Bulletin's statistics are frozen the day BEFORE the meeting it follows and arrive ~15 days stale, and the staff projections it 'integrates' were published in full on decision day itself (projections index confirms 11 Sep 2025, 19 Mar 2026, 11 Jun 2026 all landing on meeting Day 2). Its only genuinely new content is the boxes and the article. Sequencing note for whoever pulses it: 2026-09-24 is a heavily contaminated date — trump-xi-summit-2026-09-24 (impact HIGH), treasury-7y-note-2026-09-24, treasury-buyback-20y30y-2026-09-24, new-home-sales-2026-09-24 and scoos-2026-09-24 all share it, with durable-goods-2026-09-25 the next morning. Nothing on 09-24 may be credited to a Bulletin whose numbers were fixed on ~09-09. Estimate; it widens caution and licenses nothing.
